claim: In the same two-dimensional GCMC model (reservoir at 0.5% area fraction) with E_AA = 0, E_AB = 7.0 kT and E_BB = 1.6 kT, the free-energy landscape over crystal size and lattice symmetry has a square (checkerboard) minimum at small sizes and a hexagonal (stripe) minimum at large sizes, so a square crystal nucleates first and turns hexagonal as it grows, by a diffusionless rearrangement: a two-step pathway between two crystals. With E_BB = 0 (E_AB = 7.0 kT) the checkerboard, and with E_AB = 6.3 kT and E_BB = 3.5 kT the honeycomb, is favoured at every size and crystallisation is one-step.

validity_conditions: A MODEL RESULT, NOT A MEASUREMENT ON COLLOIDS. Two dimensions; grand canonical Monte Carlo with the authors' own C++ code, not HOOMD; periodic box 53.3 x 53.3 particle diameters; the pair potential is Rogers and Crocker's measured DNA-hybridisation potential with its range rescaled to about 5% of the diameter; A-A pairs never bind (E_AA = 0); reservoir at 0.5% area fraction with equal chemical potentials for A and B; insertion/deletion and species-flip moves once per 1,000 displacements on average; at least 2e10 displacement trials per run; no hydrodynamics. Landscapes from umbrella sampling with WHAM in crystal size and the symmetry parameter Phi = (2/pi) arctan(Psi6/Psi4); 200 unbiased runs started at saddle points follow the landscape. The paper's reading of the mechanism: a two-step path appears when one phase has the lower effective bulk free energy but the higher effective surface free energy; its fitted bulk and surface densities are in the Supplementary Information and are not entered. A preliminary HOOMD-blue molecular-dynamics check (set-up not in the file) also shows the checkerboard-to-stripe transition, which the authors take as evidence it is not a Monte Carlo artefact. Well depths are in kT and so appear in numbers, not validity.
